correctness.rationale: With \(s=1-q\), set \(X=s^{T_0}\) and \(\phi(x)=x\log x/\log s\). The lattice points satisfy \(\phi(s^t)=ts^t\), and their piecewise-linear interpolant through \((0,0)\) is concave because \(\phi\) is strictly concave. Therefore at fixed \(E X=p\), Jensen gives the sharp maximum \(M_+=L(p)\), attained exactly by the two adjacent lattice points \(s^k,s^{k+1}\). Pointwise \(T_0s^{T_0}\ge s^{T_0}\) gives \(M\ge p\), with equality only at the boundary \(T_0=1\); a law on \(\{1,N\}\) with its mixing weight chosen to preserve \(p\) makes \(M\downarrow p\). Convex mixing of fixed-p laws fills the interval. Substitution into the published affine variance identity reverses the endpoints and gives the complete variance envelope.

source_inspections.title: On Completion Times under Memoryless Catastrophe
source_inspections.trigger: Exact same catastrophe model and source of the mean/variance formulas.

value.rationale: Fixing one-attempt success probability fixes the mean but not the variance, so the exact remaining fluctuation range is a natural question for restart/catastrophe models. The theorem solves that support-constrained moment problem completely, identifies both extremal mechanisms and shows the discrete lattice changes the Jensen envelope.

final_claim: For memoryless catastrophe with fixed catastrophe probability \(q\) and fixed one-attempt success probability \(p=g(1-q)\), the restarted completion-time variance has exactly the interval stated in RESULT.md: its minimum is attained by the adjacent two-point base completion law determined by \(p\), while the supremum is approached by two-point laws on \(\{1,N\}\); equivalently \(M=(1-q)g'(1-q)\) has exact range \((p,M_+]\) for \(p<1-q\), with the stated degenerate boundary at \(p=1-q\).
limitations: Positive-integer base completion time and independent geometric catastrophe only.
The variance supremum is not attained when \(p<1-q\).
